title: Two balls with strictly separated brackets share no point of the real line
statement: If the upper bracket of one basic ball is strictly below the lower bracket of another -- ofRat (q + 1/(k+1)) < ofRat (r - 1/(m+1)) -- then no real number lies in both. This is the geometric half of Hausdorff separation for the open-ball frame of R, and it is deliberately recorded as the half that IS proved. Four steps and no arithmetic: CReal.le_trans through the shared point turns the two memberships into ofRat (r - 1/(m+1)) <= ofRat (q + 1/(k+1)), CReal.lt_of_le_of_lt composes that against the separation hypothesis, and CReal.lt_irrefl closes it. The missing half is index selection rather than geometry: producing the separated pair from CReal.Apart x y means eliminating the Or, reading CReal.lt's rational gap, applying the Archimedean property and discharging two Rat inequalities. ADR-1643 sizes that at 250-400 lines of term building against lemmas that all exist, and this fact is written so a reader can see which half is which rather than inferring a stronger claim.

formal.statement: theorem Top.ball_separated : ((x0 : Rat) -> ((x1 : Rat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : CReal.lt (CReal.ofRat (Rat.add x0 (Rat.natDivSucc (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) x2))) (CReal.ofRat (Rat.sub x1 (Rat.natDivSucc (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) x3)))) -> ((x5 : CReal) -> ((x6 : Top.MemBall x5 x0 x2) -> ((x7 : Top.MemBall x5 x1 x3) -> False))))))))

evidence.supports: Top.ball_separated is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement, and Kernel::axiom_footprint reports 0 assumed names.
checkers: producing-build (Kernel::add_declaration, which re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example top_frame_theorem_inventory -- Top.ball_separated | grep -cE '^theorem[[:space:]]+Top\.ball_separated[[:space:]]+8[[:space:]]+0[[:space:]]'
evidence.notes: The exit status depends on the finding three times over. top_frame_theorem_inventory exits NON-ZERO when the filter matches nothing (asking for a declaration and finding none is a failure, not an empty report) AND when any printed row carries a nonempty axiom footprint. grep -c then exits 1 printing 0 unless the anchored row is present with the recorded binder count and a footprint column of exactly 0. Anchored with [[:space:]], never a backslash-t: in a scripted (GNU) grep that is a literal t, and 68 checkers in this ledger were wrong for exactly that reason. grep -c rather than grep -q, which would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail. --release is MANDATORY: this binary builds creal underneath Top, which overflows the default debug thread stack. Definition rows need --defs and are off by default, so a caller who forgets that reads a false ABSENT rather than a wrong type.

evidence.supports: The separation hypothesis is load-bearing and its DIRECTION is what carries the proof: handed the reversed inequality -- ofRat (r - 1/(m+1)) < ofRat (q + 1/(k+1)), which is true precisely when the two balls DO overlap -- the same proof term is refused by Kernel::add_declaration, while the forward direction is accepted at the same call site. Without this the theorem could be vacuously true of a hypothesis nothing satisfies.
checkers: top_frame::top_frame_tests, run against a freshly built kernel environment
evidence.checker_command: cargo test --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib -- top_frame::top_frame_tests::ball_separation_needs_the_hypothesis_in_the_right_direction --test-threads=4 2>&1 | grep -cE '^test result: ok\. 1 passed'
evidence.notes: The `1 passed` is load-bearing: `cargo test -- <filter>` runs ZERO tests and exits 0 when the filter matches nothing, so a rename would turn this checker green while checking nothing. Requiring the exact count is what makes the exit status depend on the finding. --release is mandatory (the creal prelude overflows the debug thread stack); --test-threads=4 keeps the shared build off the OOM ceiling. Mutation MUT-E (2026-09-05) makes the control ignore its `reversed` flag; it kills exactly this one test of the eleven.

provenance.source: Lane `frame-carrier`, roadmap W2-21, executing ADR-1602's pointfree recommendation and decided in ADR-1643 (docs/research/09-decisions/adr-1643-the-frame-carrier-is-nat-indexed-and-the-ball-index-is-not-a-nat.md). formal.statement is Kernel::render_lean of the declaration's type, taken verbatim from the unfiltered emit of `top_frame_theorem_inventory --defs`; axiom_footprint is that tool's footprint column, which reads Kernel::axiom_footprint.

notes: The conclusion is False, so the reader's first question should be whether the hypotheses are satisfiable at all -- a theorem with an unsatisfiable premise is worthless and an empty axiom footprint would not notice. Top.ball_mem_self (a ball contains its own centre) is the non-vacuity witness for Top.MemBall, and F:top-open-ball-frame-covers-the-real-line is the witness that the balls cover R, which is why it is the depends_on.
